chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Abdul Salam ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Nuaym, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I entered the Obligatory Tawaaf but could not begin with anything from the supplications except for the sending of Blessings upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) (Salawat), and I performed the Sa'ee, so that was that (as well)'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No one from the beseechers would be Given anything superior that what you would be Given'.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of sending blessings upon the Prophet and his family during Hajj rituals according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Abd al-Salam ibn al-Rahman ibn Nu'aym reports to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that during his Hajj rituals, he found himself unable to recite specific supplications, relying solely on sending blessings upon the Prophet and his family (Salawat) during both Tawaaf and Sa'ee. The Imam affirmed this, stating that receiving the reward of Salawat is the highest gift given to any supplicant. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that Salawat serves as a comprehensive key to divine acceptance, often surpassing the merit of lengthy verbal supplications when recited with sincerity.
